hooks.name: Unsafe Review on FFI Edits
hooks.description: Mirrors the security-review hook for FFI code: when a file in any rustconn-*-sys crate is saved, invokes the unsafe-reviewer sub-agent to audit SAFETY comments, precondition guards, panic boundaries and the unsafe budget. Read-only. These four crates hold the only sanctioned unsafe in the workspace and had no hook coverage at all until now, while credential code has had it since the security-review hook landed.

action.prompt:
A file in a rustconn-*-sys crate was just edited. These are the only crates in the workspace allowed to contain `unsafe`, so a change here is the highest-risk edit in the repo.

Invoke the `unsafe-reviewer` sub-agent. Use invokeSubAgent with name "unsafe-reviewer" and a prompt like: "Review the recently edited rustconn-*-sys file(s). Verify: (1) every `unsafe` block has a `// SAFETY:` comment directly above it, not separated by intervening code; (2) each SAFETY comment names the invariant AND why it holds here, rather than asserting safety; (3) any precondition guard the comment cites actually runs before the unsafe call; (4) pointer/descriptor validity where applicable; (5) no panic can unwind across an FFI boundary, especially in `pre_exec` hooks that run in the forked child; (6) FFI type fidelity and `#[repr(C)]`; (7) thread-safety claims are argued, not asserted; (8) report the per-crate `unsafe` count and flag any newly added block prominently. Do not ask for Miri — it cannot execute these syscalls; ask for a contract test asserting the precondition guard instead."

Report the sub-agent's findings. If it reports no issues, a one-line confirmation plus the unsafe count is enough.

If the sub-agent is not available in your tool set, do the review yourself against the same eight checks — steering `#code-review` describes how this pass composes with the others.
